FQN: Example: Control QR Code version and error correction level with QrOptions
Kind: verified_example
Provenance: authored
Verification: passed
Authored example: written for foss-mcp against the pinned library, not taken from the upstream README; published only after the ingestion verifier compiled or ran it against that commit.
Verification-Level: ran-exit0
Verified-With: Python 3.13.16

Written against the public API surface (no single upstream sample demonstrates this); the upstream samples only use QR Code at its default settings. Generates a default QR Code, then an explicit version-5, error-correction-level-H QR Code, and checks the resulting module grid is square and matches the ISO/IEC 18004 size formula for version 5.

Example:
# Authored example: control QR Code version and error correction level with QrOptions.
from aspose_barcode_foss import QrEncodeMode, QrErrorCorrectionLevel, QrOptions, qr

default_barcode = qr("PAYLOAD")
default_size = default_barcode.symbol.matrix.width
print("default version size:", default_size)

explicit_barcode = qr(
    "PAYLOAD",
    encode=QrOptions(
        version=5,
        error_correction_level=QrErrorCorrectionLevel.H,
        encoding_mode=QrEncodeMode.ALPHANUMERIC,
    ),
)
matrix = explicit_barcode.symbol.matrix
print("explicit version=5 size:", matrix.width, matrix.height)

# Each QR version adds 4 modules per side over the previous one (ISO/IEC 18004: 21 + 4*(version-1)).
expected_size = 21 + 4 * (5 - 1)
assert matrix.width == expected_size
assert matrix.height == expected_size
assert matrix.width > default_size
print("OK")

FQN: Doc: Scope and Limitations
Known issues, unsupported functionality, and other troubleshooting-relevant scope boundaries for Aspose.BarCode FOSS for Python, straight from its README at the pinned commit:

- This library only generates (encodes) barcodes — it does not read or decode existing barcode
  images for any symbology.
- PDF rendering is not implemented — `Barcode.to_pdf()` and `PdfRenderer.render()` both raise
  NotImplementedError. SVG and PNG rendering are implemented for every symbology.
- ECI (Extended Channel Interpretation) normalization and validation (EciHelper.normalize/
  `.validate`) are not implemented in this FOSS build, even though `EncodeOptions` exposes an
  eci_assignment_number field on every symbology's options type.
- GS1 data parsing and validation (Gs1Helper.parse/`.validate`) are not implemented in this FOSS
  build, even though `EncodeOptions` exposes a gs1_enabled field on every symbology's options
  type.

For PDF rendering and additional symbologies, see
[Aspose.BarCode for Python — Enterprise Edition](https://products.aspose.com/barcode/python-net/),
which adds the full commercial rendering pipeline and broader symbology coverage on top of this
FOSS API surface.
Source-Commit: 06eca5c01e13ed6d59a640f1cf330c1c5a57d151

FQN: Doc: Installation, Dependencies, and Quick Start
The package is not yet published to PyPI. Install it from a source checkout:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/aspose-barcode-foss/Aspose.BarCode-FOSS-for-Python.git
cd Aspose.BarCode-FOSS-for-Python
pip install .
```

The distribution is named `aspose-barcode-foss`; the import package is `aspose_barcode_foss`.
Requires Python 3.12+ and Pillow >= 10.1.0 (a real, declared runtime dependency, used only for
PNG rendering) — otherwise the library has no system-level dependencies, and ships a py.typed
marker for full type-checker support.

- Pillow >=10.1.0 — used only for PNG rendering; SVG output has no third-party dependency.

- Python 3.12 or later.

- pytest >=8.0 and ruff >=0.15.7 — used only by the test suite and linter, never required to
  install or use the library.

Generate a Code 128 barcode and render it to SVG and PNG:

```python
from aspose_barcode_foss import code128

barcode = code128("Hello-World")
svg = barcode.to_svg()   # -> str
png = barcode.to_png()   # -> bytes
```

FQN: Example: Generate every supported symbology and compare their module grid shapes
Kind: verified_example
Provenance: authored
Verification: passed
Authored example: written for foss-mcp against the pinned library, not taken from the upstream README; published only after the ingestion verifier compiled or ran it against that commit.
Verification-Level: ran-exit0
Verified-With: Python 3.13.16

Adapted from the upstream examples/all_symbologies.py script. Encodes one sample per symbology through its dedicated helper and checks that the linear symbologies (Code 128, Code 39, Code 39 Extended) encode as a single module row, the retail symbologies (EAN-13, UPC-A) encode as two module rows, and QR Code encodes as a genuine square 2D matrix taller than any linear row.

Example:
# Authored example: generate every supported symbology and compare their module grid shapes.
from aspose_barcode_foss import code128, code39, code39ext, ean8, ean13, qr, upca, upce

SAMPLES = [
    ("Code 128", code128, "ABC-12345"),
    ("Code 39", code39, "ABC-123"),
    ("Code 39 Extended", code39ext, "Item #42"),
    ("EAN-13", ean13, "590123412345"),
    ("EAN-8", ean8, "1234567"),
    ("UPC-A", upca, "01234567890"),
    ("UPC-E", upce, "01234500005"),
    ("QR Code", qr, "https://example.com"),
]

shapes = {}
for label, factory, data in SAMPLES:
    matrix = factory(data).symbol.matrix
    print(f"{label:18} {data!r:18} -> {matrix.width}x{matrix.height} modules")
    shapes[label] = (matrix.width, matrix.height)

# Every linear symbology (Code 128/39) encodes as a single module row.
assert shapes["Code 128"][1] == 1
assert shapes["Code 39"][1] == 1
assert shapes["Code 39 Extended"][1] == 1
# The retail symbologies (EAN/UPC) encode as two module rows.
assert shapes["EAN-13"][1] == 2
assert shapes["UPC-A"][1] == 2
# QR Code is a genuine 2D matrix: square, and taller than any linear symbology's single row.
qr_width, qr_height = shapes["QR Code"]
assert qr_width == qr_height
assert qr_height > 1
print("OK")
Source-Commit: 06eca5c01e13ed6d59a640f1cf330c1c5a57d151

FQN: Doc: Key Capabilities and API Reference
- Code 128 barcodes encode with automatic optimal Code Set A/B/C switching, or a specific code
  set forced through `Code128Options.encode_mode`.
- Encode Code 39 barcodes in the base 43-character set or the Extended/Full-ASCII form (via
  `code39()`/`code39ext()`), with an optional modulo-43 check character.
- EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, and UPC-E retail barcodes support automatic check-digit computation or
  explicit check-digit validation via allow_check_digit_input.
- QR Code (Model 2) generation spans versions 1-40, with selectable error correction level
  (`QrErrorCorrectionLevel`) and encoding mode (`QrEncodeMode`).
- Select any symbology by name — canonical or alias — through the generic `generate()`
  (`generate(symbology, data)`) entry point, independent of the dedicated per-symbology helpers.
- Render any encoded barcode to SVG (to_svg()) or PNG (to_png()), or through a custom
  `Renderer` subclass passed to `Barcode.render()`.
- Control rendering with `RenderOptions` — scale, DPI, module width/height, quiet zone,
  foreground/background color, transparent background, and text display/font.

`Barcode` is the primary entry point: it is returned by `generate()` and every per-symbology
helper (`code128()`, `qr()`, and similar), and its to_svg()/to_png()/render() methods
produce the rendered output.

Adapted from the upstream examples/error_handling.py script. Triggers InvalidInputError for an empty Code 128 payload and for an EAN-13 payload with the wrong digit count, and SymbologyNotFoundError for an unknown symbology name passed to generate, checking each exception's real message text.

Example:
# Authored example: handle invalid input and an unknown symbology from the typed exceptions.
from aspose_barcode_foss import InvalidInputError, SymbologyNotFoundError, code128, ean13, generate

try:
    code128("")  # empty input
    raise AssertionError("expected InvalidInputError for empty Code 128 input")
except InvalidInputError as error:
    print(f"InvalidInputError: {error}")
    assert "empty" in str(error)

try:
    ean13("123")  # wrong number of digits
    raise AssertionError("expected InvalidInputError for a short EAN-13 payload")
except InvalidInputError as error:
    print(f"InvalidInputError: {error}")
    assert "12 or 13 digits" in str(error)
    assert "got 3" in str(error)

try:
    generate("datamatrix", "data")  # unknown symbology
    raise AssertionError("expected SymbologyNotFoundError for an unknown symbology")
except SymbologyNotFoundError as error:
    print(f"SymbologyNotFoundError: {error}")
    assert "datamatrix" in str(error)
print("OK")

Adapted from the upstream examples/render_options.py script. Renders a Code 128 barcode through to_svg(options=...) and through render(SvgRenderer(), options=...) directly, checks both produce identical output, that the requested foreground and background colors appear in the SVG markup, and that the styled output differs from the unstyled default.

Example:
# Authored example: style rendered output with RenderOptions and confirm a direct Renderer call matches the convenience wrapper.
from aspose_barcode_foss import RenderOptions, SvgRenderer, code128

barcode = code128("Hello-World")

options = RenderOptions(
    scale=2.0,
    foreground_color="#224466",
    background_color="#fff8f0",
    show_text=True,
    font_size=9.0,
)

# to_svg() is a convenience wrapper around render(SvgRenderer(), ...).
svg = barcode.to_svg(options=options)
artifact = barcode.render(SvgRenderer(), options=options)
print("artifact matches to_svg:", artifact.data == svg)
assert artifact.data == svg
assert "#224466" in svg
assert "#fff8f0" in svg

default_svg = barcode.to_svg()
print("styled output differs from the default rendering:", svg != default_svg)
assert svg != default_svg
print("OK")

FQN: Example: Generate every supported symbology and compare their module grid shapes
Kind: verified_example
Provenance: authored
Verification: passed
Authored example: written for foss-mcp against the pinned library, not taken from the upstream README; published only after the ingestion verifier compiled or ran it against that commit.
Verification-Level: ran-exit0
Verified-With: Python 3.13.16

Adapted from the upstream examples/all_symbologies.py script. Encodes one sample per symbology through its dedicated helper and checks that the linear symbologies (Code 128, Code 39, Code 39 Extended) encode as a single module row, the retail symbologies (EAN-13, UPC-A) encode as two module rows, and QR Code encodes as a genuine square 2D matrix taller than any linear row.

Example:
# Authored example: generate every supported symbology and compare their module grid shapes.
from aspose_barcode_foss import code128, code39, code39ext, ean8, ean13, qr, upca, upce

SAMPLES = [
    ("Code 128", code128, "ABC-12345"),
    ("Code 39", code39, "ABC-123"),
    ("Code 39 Extended", code39ext, "Item #42"),
    ("EAN-13", ean13, "590123412345"),
    ("EAN-8", ean8, "1234567"),
    ("UPC-A", upca, "01234567890"),
    ("UPC-E", upce, "01234500005"),
    ("QR Code", qr, "https://example.com"),
]

shapes = {}
for label, factory, data in SAMPLES:
    matrix = factory(data).symbol.matrix
    print(f"{label:18} {data!r:18} -> {matrix.width}x{matrix.height} modules")
    shapes[label] = (matrix.width, matrix.height)

# Every linear symbology (Code 128/39) encodes as a single module row.
assert shapes["Code 128"][1] == 1
assert shapes["Code 39"][1] == 1
assert shapes["Code 39 Extended"][1] == 1
# The retail symbologies (EAN/UPC) encode as two module rows.
assert shapes["EAN-13"][1] == 2
assert shapes["UPC-A"][1] == 2
# QR Code is a genuine 2D matrix: square, and taller than any linear symbology's single row.
qr_width, qr_height = shapes["QR Code"]
assert qr_width == qr_height
assert qr_height > 1
print("OK")
Source-Commit: 06eca5c01e13ed6d59a640f1cf330c1c5a57d151

# Authored example: handle invalid input and an unknown symbology from the typed exceptions.
from aspose_barcode_foss import InvalidInputError, SymbologyNotFoundError, code128, ean13, generate

try:
    code128("")  # empty input
    raise AssertionError("expected InvalidInputError for empty Code 128 input")
except InvalidInputError as error:
    print(f"InvalidInputError: {error}")
    assert "empty" in str(error)

try:
    ean13("123")  # wrong number of digits
    raise AssertionError("expected InvalidInputError for a short EAN-13 payload")
except InvalidInputError as error:
    print(f"InvalidInputError: {error}")
    assert "12 or 13 digits" in str(error)
    assert "got 3" in str(error)

try:
    generate("datamatrix", "data")  # unknown symbology
    raise AssertionError("expected SymbologyNotFoundError for an unknown symbology")
except SymbologyNotFoundError as error:
    print(f"SymbologyNotFoundError: {error}")
    assert "datamatrix" in str(error)
print("OK")

Adapted from the upstream examples/render_options.py script. Renders a Code 128 barcode through to_svg(options=...) and through render(SvgRenderer(), options=...) directly, checks both produce identical output, that the requested foreground and background colors appear in the SVG markup, and that the styled output differs from the unstyled default.

Example:
# Authored example: style rendered output with RenderOptions and confirm a direct Renderer call matches the convenience wrapper.
from aspose_barcode_foss import RenderOptions, SvgRenderer, code128

barcode = code128("Hello-World")

options = RenderOptions(
    scale=2.0,
    foreground_color="#224466",
    background_color="#fff8f0",
    show_text=True,
    font_size=9.0,
)

# to_svg() is a convenience wrapper around render(SvgRenderer(), ...).
svg = barcode.to_svg(options=options)
artifact = barcode.render(SvgRenderer(), options=options)
print("artifact matches to_svg:", artifact.data == svg)
assert artifact.data == svg
assert "#224466" in svg
assert "#fff8f0" in svg

default_svg = barcode.to_svg()
print("styled output differs from the default rendering:", svg != default_svg)
assert svg != default_svg
print("OK")

FQN: Example: Control QR Code version and error correction level with QrOptions
Kind: verified_example
Provenance: authored
Verification: passed

Written against the public API surface (no single upstream sample demonstrates this); the upstream samples only use QR Code at its default settings. Generates a default QR Code, then an explicit version-5, error-correction-level-H QR Code, and checks the resulting module grid is square and matches the ISO/IEC 18004 size formula for version 5.

Example:
# Authored example: control QR Code version and error correction level with QrOptions.
from aspose_barcode_foss import QrEncodeMode, QrErrorCorrectionLevel, QrOptions, qr

default_barcode = qr("PAYLOAD")
default_size = default_barcode.symbol.matrix.width
print("default version size:", default_size)

explicit_barcode = qr(
    "PAYLOAD",
    encode=QrOptions(
        version=5,
        error_correction_level=QrErrorCorrectionLevel.H,
        encoding_mode=QrEncodeMode.ALPHANUMERIC,
    ),
)
matrix = explicit_barcode.symbol.matrix
print("explicit version=5 size:", matrix.width, matrix.height)

# Each QR version adds 4 modules per side over the previous one (ISO/IEC 18004: 21 + 4*(version-1)).
expected_size = 21 + 4 * (5 - 1)
assert matrix.width == expected_size
assert matrix.height == expected_size
assert matrix.width > default_size
print("OK")
Source-Commit: 06eca5c01e13ed6d59a640f1cf330c1c5a57d151
